items.prompt: The three currencies a run is booked in are:
options: tokens, actor units, money — with money `unmeasured` until prices are captured into a config, never guessed
items.explanation: Booking all three with declared approximations; unmeasured is a respectable value for the money column until a captured price table upgrades it. (obj-23-a)

items.prompt: When is a ledger row written?
options: Once per run, as a total
At nightly reconciliation, building the digest
At SPEND time, append-only — the spend-to-book window is where overruns hide, and the budget rule reads the ledger, never a cached counter
items.explanation: Append at spend time; a counter can drift from reality, the ledger IS the reality. (obj-23-a)

items.prompt: Why is '1 actor run = 1 unit' printed on receipts?
options: Because it is a DECLARED approximation (units_source) — real per-actor pricing varies; when the approximation misleads, you upgrade the unit definition with a visible change
items.explanation: Approximations are declared at the unit, not discovered at the total — the receipt tells you which accounting world you are reading. (obj-23-a)

items.prompt: A budget cap fires mid-run at 03:00. What lands in the morning digest?
options: A request to raise the cap automatically
Nothing — the run stopped; silence is correct
An over_budget refusal line WITH the numbers and the coverage cost ('2 sources skipped pending approval') — escalation, not shutdown; coverage stays visible so the world doesn't quietly shrink
items.explanation: The cap gates the DECISION to spend and escalates with evidence: a budget that silently swallows work is a drift amplifier. (obj-23-b)
